comments.author: @Rob_Wolvin
comments.text: I can't understand why so many in academia refuse to even consider evidence of early peoples in N. America OR substantive Norse presence. WHY are these possibilities so threatening to so many? I thought scientists were all about exclusively taking an investigation where EVER the evidence leads. PERIOD.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: I understand the frustration, but the video shows why the distinction matters. Bluefish Caves was dismissed for years, then re-examined with better methods and published as evidence of human activity around 24,000 years ago. The Baffin Island material is still debated because the same objects can support more than one interpretation. Scientists should follow the evidence, but they also have to separate strong evidence from cases like Beardmore, where a genuine Norse sword was attached to a fabricated Canadian discovery story.
